article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Indica / 40% Sativa
Genetics: Big Buddha Cheese × God Bud
Breeder: Big Buddha Seeds
THC Content: 16–20%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: caryophyllene , myrcene , limonene
Primary Flavors: Cheese, lavender, tart berries, pine
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–11 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late October to early November
Indoor Yield: 200 g+
Outdoor Yield: 1,000 g+
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Cheesus combines two cannabis traditions that developed thousands of miles apart: the pungent Cheese genetics of Britain and the dense, resin-heavy God Bud family from Canada. Big Buddha Seeds created the hybrid by taking its established Big Buddha Cheese and crossing it with a selected male God Bud originating from BC Bud Depot seed stock. The resulting marijuana carries the unmistakable savory depth of Cheese but pushes the aroma into stranger territory, adding frankincense, lavender, pine, tart berries, and dark fruit.

Its effects follow a similarly layered path, beginning with noticeable euphoria before developing into a more substantial physical stone. Big Buddha Seeds classifies Cheesus as 60% indica and 40% sativa and describes the experience as euphoric and stoned, with an indoor flowering period of nine to eleven weeks. For consumers who enjoy classic Cheese weed but want additional floral, fruity, and resinous complexity, Cheesus offers a distinctive branch of the family rather than a simple recreation of the original UK clone.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder-confirmed genetics are Big Buddha Cheese × God Bud. Big Buddha Seeds explains that a prized God Bud male was selected from seeds originating with BC Bud Depot in Canada and crossed with the Big Buddha Cheese clone to produce the first Cheesus hybrids. That paternal selection brings substantial Canadian indica influence into a genetic line already rooted heavily in Skunk and Afghan cannabis. BC Bud Depot lists God Bud itself as approximately 75% indica and 25% sativa, with a deeper ancestry of God × Hawaiian × Purple Skunk.

The Cheese side is equally important. Big Buddha Seeds traces the development of its famous Cheese seed line to a clone-only Skunk No. 1 female crossed with a pure Afghani male, followed by selective backcrossing to reinforce the pungent aroma, flavor, and physical characteristics associated with Cheese. Cheesus therefore contains more genetic depth than its simple two-parent formula suggests. Skunk, Afghani , Hawaiian, Purple Skunk, and God Bud ancestry all contribute to the finished hybrid. Those components help explain why the strain can smell simultaneously savory, floral, resinous, fruity, and incense-like rather than expressing the straightforward dairy funk associated with some Cheese cultivars.
Effects and Experience

Cheesus generally begins with a noticeable upward shift in mood. The first portion of the experience can feel cheerful, mentally loose, and pleasantly euphoric, making conversation, music, movies, or an unstructured evening more absorbing. Big Buddha Seeds summarizes the effect as an “euphoric stoned” experience, which captures the unusual balance well: the cultivar does not behave like a purely cerebral sativa, but neither does it immediately produce the heavy lethargy of a highly sedating indica.

Physical effects become more obvious as time passes. Shoulders and limbs can feel heavier, activity becomes less urgent, and the experience gradually settles into a fuller body stone. At moderate amounts, there may still be enough mental brightness for socializing or creative entertainment. Larger servings are more likely to produce haziness, reduced motivation, and a desire to remain seated. Commercial examples are frequently reported in the mid-to-upper teens or around 20% THC, but cannabinoid concentration is not fixed by genetics alone. Growing environment, phenotype, harvest maturity, curing, and laboratory methodology can all change measured potency, so the tested label on the actual flower should take precedence over a strain-wide THC estimate.
Medical Benefits

The combination of mood elevation and progressive bodily relaxation may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer a cultivar that does not begin with immediate sedation. Some people choose weed with this type of effect during periods of stress, reduced appetite, muscular tension, or general discomfort, particularly later in the day when becoming more relaxed is desirable. The euphoric phase may temporarily shift attention away from negative mood, while the heavier second stage can encourage rest.

Big Buddha Seeds historically promoted Cheesus as possessing medicinal qualities, but that breeder description should not be interpreted as clinical evidence that the cultivar treats a specific condition. No controlled trials have established Cheesus itself as a treatment for chronic pain, insomnia, anxiety, depression, or another disorder. THC-rich cannabis can also produce unwanted effects including dizziness, dry mouth, impaired coordination, anxiety, or excessive sedation. Medical consumers should therefore consider the cannabinoid profile of the specific batch and consult appropriate healthcare professionals when using marijuana to manage ongoing symptoms.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Frankincense is one of the most unusual elements in Cheesus. Big Buddha Seeds specifically describes the smell as deep, dank frankincense while characterizing the taste as lavender with tart fruitiness. Those qualities sit over the pungent Cheese foundation, creating an aroma that can shift between savory funk, incense smoke, dried flowers, berries, evergreen resin, and damp earth. It is considerably more perfumed than many UK Cheese descendants, yet enough Skunk-derived pungency remains to make the flower unmistakably cannabis.

On inhalation, tart berry and lavender notes can appear earlier than expected, followed by pine, earthy resin, and a lingering cheesy finish. Certain flowers may emphasize the dairy-Skunk character, while others lean more heavily toward God Bud’s fruit and floral expression. A universal terpene profile has not been published by Big Buddha Seeds, so fixed terpene percentages would create false precision. Caryophyllene would fit the peppery and pungent side of the bouquet, myrcene its earthy depth, pinene the evergreen character, and linalool the lavender-like impression. Actual terpene dominance requires batch-specific laboratory testing.
Growing Information

Cheesus is a photoperiod variety available in feminized form and is suitable for both indoor and outdoor gardens. Big Buddha Seeds describes the plant as requiring attentive cultivation rather than being completely hands-off, making it better suited to growers who can maintain stable lighting, nutrition, temperature, and humidity throughout bloom. Plants typically develop dense, resinous flowers over a flowering cycle of approximately nine to eleven weeks. The Cheese heritage contributes vigorous branching and considerable odor, while God Bud can reinforce flower density and resin production.

Indoor growers should provide good airflow around developing flowers and support heavier branches as bloom progresses. Topping or low-stress training can help distribute the canopy beneath the lights, particularly when plants are allowed a longer vegetative period. Because Cheese-family cannabis can produce exceptionally penetrating odor, effective ventilation and odor management become increasingly important during the second half of flowering. Big Buddha Seeds currently lists indoor production as 200 g+ but does not specify a standardized area or plant-count basis for that figure, so it is best interpreted as breeder production guidance rather than a guaranteed yield.

Outdoor plants have considerably greater production potential. The breeder lists harvest around the end of October to early November and gives a potential outdoor yield of 1,000 g+ in favorable conditions. Reaching those figures requires substantial sunlight, root space, a long enough autumn, and healthy plants grown to significant size. The relatively late finish may be challenging in rainy northern climates because dense buds approaching maturity can become vulnerable to mold. Growers in humid regions should watch flower interiors carefully and maintain as much airflow as possible near harvest.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Cheesus?
Cheesus is Big Buddha Cheese × God Bud. Big Buddha Seeds selected a male God Bud from BC Bud Depot Canadian seed stock and crossed it with its Big Buddha Cheese line.
Is Cheesus indica or sativa?

Big Buddha Seeds classifies Cheesus as approximately 60% indica and 40% sativa. The effects reflect that balance, combining an initially euphoric mental state with a progressively stronger body stone.
What does Cheesus taste like?

The breeder highlights lavender and tart fruit, while the broader profile includes pungent Cheese, berries, pine, spice, and earthy resin. Its aroma is especially distinctive because Big Buddha Seeds describes it as having a deep frankincense quality.
How long does Cheesus take to flower?
Indoor flowering takes approximately nine to eleven weeks. Outdoor plants generally reach maturity around late October or early November in the Northern Hemisphere.
How much can Cheesus yield?

Big Buddha Seeds currently lists indoor production at 200 g+ and outdoor potential at 1,000 g+. The breeder does not provide enough context to treat those figures as guaranteed standardized yields, and real production depends heavily on plant size, environment, lighting, training, and grower experience.
Final Thoughts on Cheesus

Cheesus works because neither side of its lineage disappears into the cross. Big Buddha Cheese supplies the old-school Skunk funk and savory depth that made British Cheese genetics famous, while God Bud brings floral sweetness, fruit, resin, and a heavier Canadian indica character. The finished marijuana smells less like conventional Cheese than the name might imply, developing an unusual combination of frankincense, lavender, tart berries, pine, earth, and pungent cannabis.

For growers, nine to eleven weeks of flowering is a reasonable tradeoff for dense flowers and potentially substantial production, particularly outdoors where Big Buddha Seeds lists yields exceeding a kilogram under favorable conditions. For consumers, the progression from euphoria toward a deeper physical stone gives this marijuana strain enough balance to remain enjoyable without feeling one-dimensional. Cheesus is ultimately best suited to enthusiasts who appreciate classic Cheese-family weed but want a more floral, fruity, and incense-heavy interpretation backed by genuine Big Buddha and BC Bud Depot genetics.
